patch.value: Require edit permission for package catalog mutations in pm-web

The new per-project package catalog routes verified that the caller HAD access to a project but not that the access was WRITABLE. verifyProjectAccess returns a permission field of 'edit' (owner, or an edit share) or 'view' (a view-only share), and the extensions router discarded it.

Consequence: a collaborator holding a view-only share could install, activate, deactivate and uninstall packages on someone else's project. Installing a package changes the workspace for every collaborator, so this is an edit-level action; routes/pm.ts already enforces exactly this for item mutations at line 160 and the new router did not mirror it.

Fix: added requireEditableProject(), which resolves the project and rejects a non-edit permission with 403 before any pm command is spawned. Applied to all four mutating routes (install, activate, deactivate, uninstall). The GET listing deliberately stays at read access, so a view-only collaborator can still see which packages a project uses.

Also removed a redundant resolveNpmSpec(entry.name) lookup guarded by a non-null assertion; the matched catalog entry already carries its own npmSpec constant, so the spawn argument comes straight from the catalog.
A view-only collaborator receives 403 on every package mutation and no pm command is spawned, while still being able to list the catalog.

All four mutating routes return 403 for a view-only share and the spawn log stays empty; GET returns 200. Negative-controlled: removing the permission check turns the new test red on the first install attempt, so the gate cannot pass vacuously. 156 tests pass, typecheck clean.
Fixed by requiring edit permission on all four mutating catalog routes, with a negative-controlled regression test covering view-only shares.
